  PROBLEM: This contradicts the behavior this PR adds in `scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh`. The CI side channel (`PR_CHECKS_LAST_CI_STATE`) now drops a cancelled run when a newer bound run of the same name supersedes it and `PR_CHECKS_CI_RUN_IDS` is set. So not every run with that name counts any more.
  WHY: It does not fail at runtime. An operator reading the README would expect a cancelled CI `lint` to keep the auto-merge wait in a failed state even after a successful re-run. The code now lets the re-run unblock the wait.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The most recent autofix editor summary (PR comment 6137380697, 2026-10-13T03:14:01Z) states the editor "corrected the `AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK` row (line 127)" in `README.md` because that row used to say "every run with that name counts", which this PR made untrue — it now must also say that a cancelled run is dropped when a newer run of the same name replaces it, provided both runs are bound to `AUTO_MERGE_WAIT_WORKFLOWS` runs on the head.
  Expected change site: `README.md` (line 127, the `AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK` row in the variables table).
  Evidence of absence: `README.md` is not in `pr_changed_files.txt`; a direct read of `README.md` line 127 still contains the now-incorrect clause "Every run with that name counts and the review's own run never does, so an earlier `review / gate` success cannot stand in for CI." The auto-merge wait now drops a cancelled run only when a newer bound run supersedes it (per `scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh` `_pr_wait_for_required_checks` and the LAST RUN's CI-side-channel edits), so the README description contradicts the implementation operators and consumers will read.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The same editor summary (PR comment 6137380697) states the editor added `test_cancelled_ci_check_not_superseded_when_bound_ids_empty` to `tests/test_pr_checks_lib_required_filter.py`, which sets `PR_CHECKS_CI_RUN_IDS=""` and checks that a newer `lint` from a different Actions run does not replace a cancelled CI `lint`, so the gate still blocks.
  Expected change site: `tests/test_pr_checks_lib_required_filter.py` (a new test function named `test_cancelled_ci_check_not_superseded_when_bound_ids_empty`).
  Evidence of absence: a grep of `tests/test_pr_checks_lib_required_filter.py` for `PR_CHECKS_CI_RUN_IDS` returns seven matches, none of which reference the test name claimed in the editor summary; a regex search across `tests/` for `bound_ids_empty|empty.*bound|bound.*empty` returns no matches. The other new tests in the same LAST RUN (`test_cancelled_ci_check_not_superseded_by_other_workflow_same_name`, `test_cancelled_ci_check_superseded_by_rerun_of_same_actions_run`, `test_cancelled_ci_check_superseded_by_newer_bound_ci_run_only`, `test_non_ci_names_keep_cross_run_supersession`) all use `PR_CHECKS_CI_RUN_IDS` either explicitly or by inheriting the env that has it unset, but none pins `PR_CHECKS_CI_RUN_IDS=""` to pin the strict-mode bound sentinel that the LAST RUN's lib code relies on (`${PR_CHECKS_CI_RUN_IDS-__unbound__}` expands to `__unbound__` when the var is unset or empty, and only that sentinel exercises the strict rule without running through `__unbound__`'s `keep every run` path). Without this regression test, future edits that drop the empty-string-or-unset distinction could silently re-introduce the "another workflow's `lint` hides a cancelled CI `lint`" hole this PR closes.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
